title: Verb + object + infinitive patterns
titleVi: Cấu trúc động từ + tân ngữ + nguyên mẫu
summary: tell/advise/persuade somebody to do, make/let + động từ nguyên mẫu, và see somebody do/doing.
whyItMatters: Cấu trúc *động từ + tân ngữ + to V* là xương sống của câu học thuật: *The policy encourages firms to invest*, *Students are required to attend*. Nhưng chỉ một nhóm động từ dùng được cấu trúc này; nhóm khác cần mệnh đề *that*. Nhầm nhóm là lỗi ngữ pháp nặng, và lỗi *suggest me to do* xuất hiện trong phần lớn bài Writing band 6.5.

sections.heading: Verb + object + to-infinitive: the persuasion group
body: These verbs need a person between the verb and the infinitive: **tell, advise, remind, warn, invite, encourage, persuade, force, teach, allow, enable, expect, ask, want, would like**. *The tutor advised me to rewrite the introduction.*

The object is not optional. *She advised to rewrite* is incomplete English; you must say who was advised. The only exception is when the object is obvious from context in very informal speech, which is not a register you want in Task 2.

**get** works in the same slot with a more informal flavour: *I got my brother to check the figures.* **enable** and **allow** sound formal and are ideal for describing policy effects: *Flexible hours enable parents to combine work and childcare.*

rows: tell / ask
The editor asked me to cut 200 words.
advise / recommend (that)
My tutor advised me to narrow the topic.
remind / warn
The sign warns visitors not to feed the animals.
encourage / persuade
The scheme encourages households to insulate their homes.
force / get
Rising rents forced many families to move out.
allow / enable
Online portals enable citizens to track applications.
expect / want / would like
Voters expect the government to act quickly.
teach / show
The course teaches students how to read critically.

sections.heading: Verbs that refuse the pattern
body: A second group cannot take *object + to-infinitive*. They need a **that-clause** or a preposition: **suggest, recommend, propose, insist, explain, complain, apologise, admit, deny, announce**.

*She suggested that I apply early* or *She suggested applying early* — never *She suggested me to apply*. *He explained the rule to me* — never *explained me the rule*. *They insisted on paying* — never *insisted me to pay*.
This is a lexical fact, not a logic problem: *advise* and *suggest* mean similar things but belong to different pattern groups. Learn them with their pattern attached.

examples.right: The report recommends that the city invest in cycle lanes.
examples.wrong: The report recommends the city to invest in cycle lanes.

examples.right: She explained the procedure to the new staff.
examples.wrong: She explained the new staff the procedure.
examples.note: **explain something to somebody**, never two objects.

examples.right: They insisted on checking every document.

sections.heading: make, let and help: no to
body: **make** and **let** take the **bare infinitive** — no *to*: *The film made me cry*, *My manager let me leave early*. **help** accepts both: *She helped me (to) carry the boxes.*

In the passive, *make* takes *to* back: *He was made to apologise.* *Let* has no natural passive, so English uses **be allowed to** or **be permitted to**: *Students are not allowed to use phones in the exam hall.*
**had better**, **would rather** and **why not** also take the bare infinitive, which is why *We'd better to leave* is wrong.

rows: The law makes employers provide safety training.
Employers are made to provide safety training.
They let visitors park for free.
Visitors are allowed to park for free.
The scheme helped residents (to) reduce bills.
Residents were helped to reduce their bills.
Nothing made him change his mind.
He could not be made to change his mind.

sections.heading: see somebody do / see somebody doing
body: Perception verbs — **see, hear, watch, notice, feel, observe** — take either the bare infinitive or the -ing form, with a real difference in meaning.

**Bare infinitive** = you saw the whole completed action: *I saw him cross the road* (from one side to the other). **-ing form** = you saw it in progress, part of it: *I saw him crossing the road* (he was in the middle of it when you looked).

In the passive, the bare infinitive becomes a to-infinitive: *He was seen to leave the building at midnight.* *She was heard singing in the corridor.* Academic writing about observation and evidence uses exactly these forms.

examples.right: Researchers observed the children share toys more readily.
Researchers observed the children sharing toys.
examples.note: Ongoing behaviour, -ing form — the more natural choice for describing a pattern.

examples.right: The suspect was seen entering the car park.
examples.wrong: The suspect was seen enter the car park.
examples.note: Passive needs **to**: *was seen to enter*; *was seen entering* is also correct.

sections.heading: Turning the pattern into academic distance
body: The *object + to-infinitive* pattern lets you describe what institutions do to people without naming an agent — very useful in Task 2: *Employees are encouraged to work from home*, *Applicants are required to provide two references*, *Households were forced to cut consumption.*

Note the reporting verbs that already carry evaluation: **require, oblige, permit, entitle, urge, prompt**. *The crisis prompted the government to intervene* is far stronger than *The government decided to intervene because of the crisis.*
One caution: do not stack two *to* patterns. *The government encouraged people to try to reduce to use cars* collapses. Keep one infinitive chain per clause and start a new sentence.

examples.right: The regulation requires airlines to offset their emissions.
Higher fees may deter students from applying.
examples.wrong: Higher fees may deter students to apply.
examples.note: *deter* belongs to the preposition group: **deter somebody from -ing**.

examples.right: The campaign urged residents to report faulty streetlights.
examples.note: **urge somebody to do** — a strong reporting verb for Task 2.

commonMistakes.wrong: My teacher suggested me to write a longer conclusion.
commonMistakes.right: My teacher suggested that I write a longer conclusion. / My teacher suggested writing a longer conclusion.
commonMistakes.why: **suggest** thuộc nhóm không nhận *tân ngữ + to V*; tiếng Việt *gợi ý tôi viết* khiến người học áp thẳng cấu trúc *advise/tell*. Phải dùng mệnh đề *that* hoặc **-ing**.

commonMistakes.wrong: My parents made me to study medicine.
commonMistakes.right: My parents made me study medicine.
commonMistakes.why: **make + tân ngữ + động từ nguyên mẫu không có to**. Người học thêm *to* vì đa số cấu trúc khác đều có.

commonMistakes.wrong: She was made apologise for the delay.
commonMistakes.right: She was made to apologise for the delay.
commonMistakes.why: Ở dạng bị động, **make** lấy lại *to*: *be made to do*. Đây là ngoại lệ duy nhất của nhóm này.

commonMistakes.wrong: I heard him to sing in the next room.
commonMistakes.right: I heard him sing in the next room. / I heard him singing in the next room.
commonMistakes.why: Động từ tri giác (**hear, see, watch**) đi với động từ nguyên mẫu hoặc **-ing**, không dùng *to* ở dạng chủ động.

commonMistakes.wrong: The manager explained me the new policy.
commonMistakes.right: The manager explained the new policy to me.
commonMistakes.why: **explain** không nhận hai tân ngữ. Tiếng Việt *giải thích cho tôi quy định mới* dịch thẳng thành *explained me*, nhưng tiếng Anh cần **explain something to somebody**.

ieltsTips: Dùng `enable/allow somebody to do` để mô tả lợi ích chính sách: `Flexible working allows employees to balance career and family.`
Dùng `be required/expected/encouraged to do` để tạo giọng văn khách quan trong Task 2 mà không cần nêu chủ thể.
Với động từ tri giác, chọn **-ing** khi mô tả hành vi lặp lại, chọn nguyên mẫu khi mô tả một hành động trọn vẹn — khác biệt này được tính vào độ chính xác ngữ pháp.
Tránh chuỗi *to V* liên tiếp; nếu câu có hai ý sai khiến, tách thành hai câu hoặc dùng mệnh đề *that*.

exercises.question: The campaign encourages households ___ less water in summer.
The committee recommended that the building ___ immediately.
exercises.explanation: Sau **recommend that** dùng dạng nguyên mẫu không *to* (subjunctive): *that the building be renovated*.

exercises.question: Passengers are not ___ to carry liquids over 100 ml.
exercises.explanation: **be allowed to do** là dạng bị động tương ứng với *let*.

exercises.question: I watched the technician ___ the machine twice before signing the form.
exercises.explanation: Hành động trọn vẹn, có kết thúc rõ ràng → động từ nguyên mẫu **check** (dạng *checking* cũng đúng ngữ pháp nhưng đổi nghĩa sang đang diễn ra).

exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: They forced us to wait outside.
They forced that we wait outside.
They forced to us wait outside.

exercises.question: The sign warns visitors ___ (not / touch) the exhibits.
Online systems enable applicants ___ (submit) documents from home.
The teacher let the class ___ (leave) ten minutes early.
exercises.explanation: **let + tân ngữ + động từ nguyên mẫu không to**.

exercises.question: She was made ___ (redo) the entire experiment.
exercises.explanation: Bị động của **make** cần *to*: *was made to redo*.

exercises.question: He explained the procedure ___ (prep) the new interns.
